prompt: A cosmic-ray spectrum has a differential spectrum N(E) ∝ E^(−2.7). What is the index of the cumulative spectrum N(>E)?
options: −1.7, since integrating raises the exponent by one
−2.7, as the exponent is unchanged by integrating
−3.7, since integrating a power law lowers the exponent by one in the cumulative form
−0.7, as the exponent rises by two when integrated
answer: −1.7, since integrating raises the exponent by one
explanation: Integrating a differential spectrum N(E) ∝ E^(−0.7) from E upward raises the exponent by one and flips the sign: N(>E) = ∫ N dE ∝ E^(−1.7).
